fields.detail: title_on_detail is assigned in step 1, which reads a per-item URL discovered only after step 0 actually runs. Not verifiable from the template alone.
product_page_url is assigned in step 1, which reads a per-item URL discovered only after step 0 actually runs. Not verifiable from the template alone.

concerns: Vendor's own preview reports success:false — the vendor itself flags this repair as failing; that alone warrants blocking until re-run clean.

Stage 1 now sets title_on_detail/product_page_url from input.recall_title/recall_url piped out of stage 0, so the detail-vs-listing corroboration check compares a value to itself — it can no longer catch a wrong listing title.

Stage 1's bad_input() guard matches literal '...' in URLs, implying truncated placeholder strings are entering the pipeline as real data; the guard hides that corruption instead of fixing where it originates.

Live re-fetch couldn't verify title_on_detail/product_page_url at all since they depend on a per-item URL only known after step 0 runs — no independent confirmation the listing-title fix works end-to-end.
date_published is still hardcoded to null in the listing parser, so that part of the original reported bug (recall_url/date_published absent) is left unresolved by this proposal.
